examples.label: Full scan looking for ColdFusion (8500) and friends
Hit the ColdFusion admin panel once found

notes: Port 8500 and /CFIDE/administrator/index.cfm are the tells. Old ColdFusion admin panels are riddled with auth-bypass/LFI CVEs, so version-fingerprint before attacking.

recommended.note: Broader web-app port sweep that surfaces ColdFusion.
Try default creds against the admin panel.

name: ColdFusion - Discovery and Admin Panel
description: ColdFusion listens on 8500 (and 80/443/1935/5500). The admin panel at /CFIDE/administrator/index.cfm and /CFIDE/, /cfdocs/ directories are the entry points; .cfm/.cfc are the app extensions. Known CVEs (e.g. CVE-2010-2861 LFI, CVE-2009-2265 upload) target older versions.

defense.why_it_works: ColdFusion exposes version information through its administrator panel at /CFIDE/administrator/index.cfm, default error pages, and known file extensions (.cfm, .cfc). Nmap probes and directory enumeration reliably identify ColdFusion version.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to the ColdFusion server. No credentials required for fingerprinting.
defense.impact: ColdFusion version identification enables targeting of known vulnerabilities: directory traversal (CVE-2010-2861), file upload bypass, authentication bypass.
defense.detection: GET requests to /CFIDE/administrator/index.cfm, /CFIDE/, /cfdocs/ from unauthenticated IPs.
defense.artifacts: Web server access log (GET /CFIDE/administrator/) | IDS alert for ColdFusion scanner patterns
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web sourcetype=access_combined (uri_path=\"/CFIDE/administrator/index.cfm\" OR uri_path=\"/cfdocs/\")
| stats count dc(uri_path) as urls by clientip, useragent, bin(_time, 1m)
| where urls>20 OR count>100
defense.sentinel_kql:
W3CIISLog
| summarize urls=dcount(csUriStem), hits=count() by cIP, csUserAgent, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where urls > 20 or hits > 100
| sort by hits desc
// coldfusion application fingerprinting/enumeration (path burst, scanner UA)
defense.prevention: Remove or restrict /CFIDE/ and /cfdocs/ from public access. Restrict the admin console to localhost or internal IPs. Suppress version in error pages.
defense.misconfiguration: ColdFusion admin console at /CFIDE/administrator/ publicly accessible, with version information disclosed via error pages and the console login.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# ColdFusion default
# /CFIDE/administrator/index.cfm accessible from 0.0.0.0
# Server header: Adobe ColdFusion 2016 Update 3
defense.secure_config:
# IIS -- restrict CFIDE to internal IPs
<location path="CFIDE/administrator">
  <system.webServer>
    <security>
      <ipSecurity allowUnlisted="false">
        <add ipAddress="10.0.0.0" subnetMask="255.0.0.0" allowed="true"/>
      </ipSecurity>
    </security>
  </system.webServer>
</location>
defense.evasion: Randomize the uploaded payload name and delete it after the shell connects; restrict activity to a single upload+trigger to limit web-log evidence.

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review IIS Web Server logs, Windows Security Event Log, Web proxy logs for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Detects a ColdFusion server and locates its admin panel:
  nmap -p- -sC -Pn <ip> --open   full scan looking for the ColdFusion port 8500
ColdFusion also uses 80/443/1935/5500; the admin console lives at /CFIDE/administrator/index.cfm and .cfm/.cfc are the app extensions - version-match it to CVEs (e.g. CVE-2010-2861 LFI) for exploitation.
